corrections.issue: Wrong speaker for part of the claim: the point that machine-learning strategies suffer when learned relationships break down was made by the host Alan Dunne, not Mark.
corrections.fix: Mark: trend following is observational, not causal; it avoids hard causal inference in macro and relies on observed price persistence. (Alan: machine-learning strategies learned from past relationships suffer when those relationships break down.)

corrections.issue: Merges two points and implies the safe-asset shortage makes Treasuries riskier; Mark says regulation/collateral demand makes Treasuries a (possibly scarce) safe asset, while FX risk and higher rate volatility are what make holding them riskier.
corrections.fix: Treasuries are a safe asset partly because regulation creates collateral demand (raising the question of a safe-asset shortage), but FX risk for foreign buyers and higher rate volatility (MOVE more volatile than VIX) make holding them riskier than before.

completeness_estimate: 0.75 - first reader caught all main themes (ERP, term premium, risk cycle, sizing, analysts, narratives, Quantica) but missed several secondary mechanisms and caveats (rate vol vs level, term premium vs stock-bond correlation, SVB duration risk, EPU noise, event jumps vs underreaction).
